marks.gloss_en: תא שמע: as the tenant owes the mezuza, so the tenant should owe the bedika
one who lets a house on the 14th: does the landlord check (the chametz is his) or the tenant (the prohibited thing stands in his domain)?
התם הא אמר רב משרשיא מזוזה חובת הדר היא -- the mezuza follows the dweller by its own rule, so nothing follows for bedika
Rav Mesharshiya: the mezuza is the dweller's obligation -- so it proves nothing about bedika
תניתוה: if all are believed about biur chametz, that is because every house is presumed checked (all are chaverim about bedika)
the adduced source: all are believed about biur chametz, even women, slaves and minors
or in the Mishnah means the evening (of the 14th); all agree
the whole day is fit for circumcision, but the vigilant come early to mitzvot -- 'and Avraham rose early in the morning'
bedika was set at nightfall because that is the hour people are found at home
and lamplight is good for checking -- a candle shows in the night what daylight would not
the claim under examination: a house let on the 14th carries the presumption that it has been checked
